top_story: A Houthi ballistic missile strike on 19 October killed at least 53 people at a Yemeni government training camp, the deadliest single attack since the civil war resumed and a sharp escalation in the group’s military pressure. By 21 October, sustained Houthi strikes had widened the sense of insecurity beyond Yemen’s front lines, prompting Washington to draw down non-essential embassy staff and families from Saudi Arabia as the threat environment spilled deeper into the Gulf. In Gaza, a different but equally consequential form of attrition is unfolding as breast cancer patients face lethal delays because hospitals are destroyed, radiotherapy is unavailable, and medical evacuations remain tightly constrained. Together, these developments show a region where armed escalation and institutional collapse are steadily converting insecurity into long-term civilian harm.
